## Tours through La Fortuna and Arenal: which itinerary should you choose?

[La Fortuna and Arenal Volcano](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/) are among the natural highlights of Costa Rican itineraries. The area offers forest trails, views of the volcanic cone from lookout points, hot springs and excursions to the [Caño Negro Wildlife Refuge](/costa-rica/place/cano-negro-wildlife-refuge/). Yet tours that mention “Arenal” vary so widely that a shared destination alone is not enough to choose between them.

In our catalog, you will find {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} that pass through this area on their main itinerary. On some journeys, La Fortuna is the base for 2–3 nature excursions; on others, it is an overnight stop between [Poás Volcano](/costa-rica/place/poas-volcano/) and [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/). Some trips continue to the ocean or across an international border.

The most important question is **what the day around Arenal actually includes**: a hike beside old lava flows, hanging bridges, hot springs, an excursion to Caño Negro, or simply a transfer and an overnight stay. For a guide to the area's geography and attractions, see the [La Fortuna and Arenal page](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/).

## How the available itineraries differ

| Itinerary | Main experiences around Arenal |
|---|---|
| [“Classic Costa Rica”](/costa-rica/tour/classic-costa-rica-san-jose-monteverde-arenal/) | Caño Negro, Lake Arenal, then Monteverde |
| [“5 Wonders of Costa Rica”](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-5-wonders/) | Hanging bridges and trails beside old lava flows |
| [“Short but Complete Tour”](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-short-complete-tour/) | Caño Negro, Río Celeste, bridges |
| [16-day private tour](/costa-rica/tour/luxury-costa-rica-16-days/) | Hot springs, lava trails and an extensive nature itinerary |
| [“Guatemala and Costa Rica”](/multi-country/tour/guatemala-costa-rica/) | Arenal alongside Mayan culture and heritage |

This is a brief comparison of the trips' main purposes, not a complete list of included services. Compare durations, terms and prices of the current programs in the table below:

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_klassicheskaya_kosta_rika,tour_source_5_chudes_kosta_riki,tour_source_lyuksovyj_tur_v_kosta_riku_na_16_dnej,tour_source_gvatemala_kosta_rika}}

### For a first visit to Costa Rica

On the [classic itinerary](/costa-rica/tour/classic-costa-rica-san-jose-monteverde-arenal/), travelers arrive in the Arenal area after visiting the [Doka coffee estate](/costa-rica/place/doka-estate/), [Poás](/costa-rica/place/poas-volcano/) and [La Paz Waterfalls](/costa-rica/place/la-paz-waterfalls/). The following day is dedicated to [Caño Negro](/costa-rica/place/cano-negro-wildlife-refuge/), before crossing Lake Arenal and continuing to Monteverde. This is a nature-focused journey emphasizing the variety of protected areas.

The [“Short but Complete Tour”](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-short-complete-tour/) also combines Arenal with Caño Negro, but adds [Río Celeste](/costa-rica/place/rio-celeste/) and a hanging-bridge walk before heading to the Pacific coast. It appeals to travelers who want nature excursions as well as free time by the ocean.

### For more forest trails and volcanic scenery

The [“5 Wonders of Costa Rica”](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-5-wonders/) itinerary devotes a separate sightseeing section to the Arenal area. On day 4, the route reaches the volcano after an introduction to Maleku culture. Day 5 includes hanging bridges and a walk along the Los Tucanes trail near old lava flows, and day 6 brings a journey across Lake Arenal toward Monteverde.

In [“3 Perspectives on Costa Rica”](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-3-perspectives/), a walk across the bridges and through lava-field areas is also scheduled after arrival from the country's central region. The journey then continues to Pacific beaches.

### For an extended nature holiday

The [16-day private itinerary](/costa-rica/tour/luxury-costa-rica-16-days/) combines [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/), Arenal, [Río Celeste](/costa-rica/place/rio-celeste/), [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/), [Manuel Antonio](/costa-rica/place/manuel-antonio/), [Corcovado](/costa-rica/place/corcovado-national-park/) and the Playa Conchal coastline. A visit to Tabacón hot springs is explicitly listed for the day of arrival at Arenal, followed later by a walk along a lava trail. This is an option for travelers who want several natural regions in one trip.

A premium classification should not be taken as a promise of every possible service. The confirmed features are the private format, listed excursions and logistics of this particular published itinerary. Check the guides, transport, accommodation and meal arrangements in the [16-day tour conditions](/costa-rica/tour/luxury-costa-rica-16-days/).

## Hanging bridges or lava trails: what is the difference?

Two popular activities around La Fortuna offer different experiences.

**[Arenal Hanging Bridges](/costa-rica/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/arenal-hanging-bridges-forest-walk/)** let you see the tropical rainforest from different heights. The main attractions are plants, birds, the forest ecosystem and views of the volcano through the trees. This walk suits travelers interested in biodiversity, although the exact trail length and difficulty should be considered when choosing a program.

**[The Los Tucanes Trail and solidified lava](/costa-rica/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/arenal-los-tucanes-lava-trail/)** focus on volcanic terrain. Ada Tours' description of the separate excursion specifies a walk in the national park's southwestern sector, near lava deposits formed after the 1968 eruption. Here you can see how vegetation gradually recolonizes old lava flows.

Both activities are available as separate excursions. But a tour's inclusion of La Fortuna **does not automatically mean that both excursions are included**. On some trips, the day near Arenal is spent traveling to Caño Negro or relaxing at hot springs.

## Can you climb to Arenal's summit?

No. **Climbing Arenal's volcanic cone is prohibited** under national park rules. SINAC restricts entry to hazardous zones around the cone and requires visitors to stay on trails open to the public. Travelers view the volcano from permitted lookout points and routes through the forest and old lava fields.

Thus, a “tour to Arenal Volcano” means a visit to the surrounding natural area, not an ascent to the crater. The 1968 eruption is part of the area's geological history; there is no basis for promising views of flowing molten lava on a present-day excursion.

The national park offers trails of varying lengths, including Las Coladas and El Ceibo. Before setting out, check which trails are open, current restrictions and visiting hours, as heavy rainfall and trail conditions may change the day's plans.

## Hot springs, Caño Negro and Monteverde

Hot springs are a separate feature of visiting La Fortuna. The [extended 16-day private tour](/costa-rica/tour/luxury-costa-rica-16-days/) explicitly includes Tabacón on the day of arrival at Arenal. In other programs, a thermal bath may be an option after the drive; unless it appears among the inclusions, it should not be regarded as a paid-for excursion.

[Caño Negro](/costa-rica/place/cano-negro-wildlife-refuge/) lies north of Arenal. Trips there generally focus on observing birds and other wildlife from a boat rather than on volcanic landscapes. An itinerary featuring Caño Negro instead of lava trails is neither better nor worse: it serves a different nature interest.

The journey to [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/) introduces another type of forest: higher in the mountains, with clouds and mist among the trees. Some tours cross Lake Arenal by boat, while others use a regular transfer. Before choosing, look at the sequence of days and the means of transportation.

For wildlife-focused trips, see [Costa Rica's nature and wildlife tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/costa-rica/). If trails, canopy activities and physical challenges appeal more, compare [adventure tours in Costa Rica](/interests/adventure/tours/costa-rica/).

## How Arenal fits into multi-country itineraries

Arenal also features in journeys through several countries. For example, [“Guatemala and Costa Rica”](/multi-country/tour/guatemala-costa-rica/) combines Guatemala's ancient cities and cultural centers with Costa Rica's natural landscapes. After a flight to San José, travelers transfer to La Fortuna, followed by [Caño Negro](/costa-rica/place/cano-negro-wildlife-refuge/) and walks over hanging bridges and along a lava trail.

The [“Costa Rica — Nicaragua” route](/multi-country/tour/costa-rica-nicaragua/) passes through Costa Rica's natural attractions before crossing into another country. In the [extended Central America itinerary](/multi-country/tour/best-of-central-america/), Arenal is just one stop among several countries. The total length of such a journey tells you little about how much time is spent near the volcano.

When comparing these trips, check how many days are allotted to La Fortuna, how the onward border crossing is organized, whether ground transfers are included, and the order of travel. You can compare country combinations in the [multi-country journeys catalog](/multi-country/).

## Weather and preparing for excursions

The Arenal area stays humid and green for much of the year. Even when Pacific beaches are dry, heavy rain can fall in La Fortuna and thick clouds can hide the volcano's summit. The clearest photographs of the cone are usually taken when visibility is good, but no one can guarantee a completely unobstructed view on a particular day.

For walks, bring closed non-slip shoes, a light rain jacket, water, and waterproof protection for documents and electronics. Some trails can become slippery after heavy rain; visitors with mobility limitations should choose an appropriate route and consider the ground surface in advance.

An important practical point is to **allow extra time when moving between regions**. The road from Arenal to Monteverde or the ocean passes through hills and mountains, so a full travel day cannot also be treated as a full sightseeing day. On multi-country trips, extra time for borders and connections matters even more.

## Frequently asked questions

### How many tours travel through La Fortuna and Arenal?

The current number is displayed in the catalog: {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The selection changes as programs are added or archived. Volcano and hanging-bridge excursions have their own separate pages.

### Which tour is suitable for a first visit to Arenal?

To discover several natural regions, compare [“Classic Costa Rica”](/costa-rica/tour/classic-costa-rica-san-jose-monteverde-arenal/) and the [“Short but Complete Tour”](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-short-complete-tour/). Their routes overlap, but they allocate time differently between Arenal, Caño Negro and the coast.

### Which tours include hanging bridges?

They are explicitly listed in [“5 Wonders of Costa Rica”](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-5-wonders/) and [“3 Perspectives on Costa Rica”](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-3-perspectives/), for example. A description of the activity itself is available on the [Arenal Hanging Bridges page](/costa-rica/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/arenal-hanging-bridges-forest-walk/).

### Can a visit to the hot springs be included?

Yes, in certain programs. For example, the [private 16-day tour](/costa-rica/tour/luxury-costa-rica-16-days/) explicitly lists Tabacón in its itinerary. For other trips, check the included services.

### Is climbing to the summit permitted?

No. The national park prohibits climbing the volcanic cone. Visitors can use authorized forest trails and viewpoints, including routes through areas of old lava flows.

### Are Arenal and Monteverde the same place?

No. [Arenal and La Fortuna](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/) are in a volcanic region, while [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/) is a highland cloud forest. Many itineraries link them, but a separate transfer is required.

## La Paz Waterfalls in Costa Rica: five cascades, forest trails and a nature park

**La Paz is a group of five waterfalls on the slopes of central Costa Rica.** The most convenient way to explore them is at La Paz Waterfall Gardens nature park, where pathways and steps lead through lush forest to viewpoints overlooking the cascades. You can spend several hours outdoors and, if you wish, add the animal and plant exhibits to your walk.

La Paz is often visited when traveling between the San José area and northern Costa Rica's natural destinations. [Poás Volcano](/costa-rica/place/poas-volcano/) is nearby, but it is a separate protected area with its own tickets and rules. If you want to visit both on the same day, allow enough time for the drive, the crater and the forest trails.

## Which waterfalls are in La Paz Waterfall Gardens?

The park has a developed route past five waterfalls: **Templo, Encantada, Magia Blanca, Escondida and La Paz**. Each occupies a different part of the forest gorge, allowing visitors to see the flowing water from various heights and angles.

One of the route's defining features is the gradual descent along pathways and stairs. There are handrails, but this is still damp forest terrain where steps may be slippery. Comfortable closed shoes with dependable grip are more useful than light beach sandals.

**La Paz is not just one roadside cascade.** The famous lower waterfall can indeed be seen from the road, but a full walk through the park takes in other cascades higher in the gorge, the forest and viewing platforms. Seeing the site from the road and from within the park are different experiences.

## What else can you do besides visiting the waterfalls?

La Paz Waterfall Gardens is a privately operated nature park with themed exhibits. These feature birds, butterflies, snakes, frogs and other animals, as well as areas dedicated to observing hummingbirds. The exhibits and forest trails offer different ways to discover Costa Rica's natural world.

It is important, however, to distinguish **animals kept in managed enclosures** from creatures living freely in the forest. Visiting an exhibit should not be presented as a guaranteed sighting of a wild jaguar or sloth along the trail. For encounters with wildlife behaving naturally, choose outings in protected natural habitats.

If waterfalls are your main interest, you can concentrate on the forest walk. Families with children and visitors interested in biology may want more time for the additional exhibits.

## How much time should you allow for La Paz?

| Visit type | What you can see |
|---|---|
| Short visit | Main waterfalls |
| Half a day | Forest and some exhibits |
| Relaxed full day | All accessible areas of the park |

The park itself recommends at least several hours, and considerably longer for a full exploration of the trails and wildlife exhibits. The time needed depends on your pace, the weather and how often you stop beside the water.

Since the route includes stairs, visitors with reduced mobility should check which viewpoints are accessible and whether the walking section can be shortened. Describing the trails as “developed” does not mean that every part is wheelchair-accessible.

## La Paz and Poás Volcano in one day

[Poás Volcano](/costa-rica/place/poas-volcano/) is known for its large crater and volcanic gases. Visits depend on volcanic activity, weather and national park rules. Unlike La Paz, access to Poás is arranged through SINAC's booking system. Park officials decide whether visitors can enter.

For a combined excursion, first check whether the volcano is accessible. If access to the crater is temporarily restricted, the waterfall visit can remain a standalone nature day, but one attraction should not be substituted for the other without agreeing on changes to the itinerary.

Another possible stop is [La Fortuna and Arenal](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/), although reaching that area requires additional driving time. Avoid planning an extensive visit to La Paz, a long volcano walk and a packed Arenal itinerary all on the same day.

## Weather and practical preparation

The forest around La Paz is humid, and a short shower is possible even in a relatively dry season. Bring a light raincoat, protection for your camera and shoes that provide firm footing on steps. There can be heavy spray near the waterfalls.

Admission to La Paz Waterfall Gardens is charged; the park operator publishes current prices and ticket inclusions. Check whether the areas you want to visit, meals and other services are included. Never plan to enter the water beneath the falls without staff permission.

We help combine La Paz with other natural attractions on your chosen itinerary. You can compare [Costa Rica tours](/costa-rica/tour/) and the [country's destinations catalog](/costa-rica/place/) separately, without assuming any particular excursion is included.

## Frequently asked questions about La Paz Waterfalls

### Are La Paz and Poás Volcano in the same park?

No. La Paz Waterfall Gardens is a separate private nature park, while Poás Volcano is within a national park. Admission and visiting rules differ.

### How many waterfalls can you see?

The developed Waterfall Gardens route includes five waterfalls. Whether the entire route can be completed depends on conditions and current park restrictions.

### Is it suitable to visit in the rain?

Light rain is normal in humid forests. Heavy rainfall makes trails and steps more slippery, so follow the guidance of park staff.

## Tours visiting La Paz Waterfalls: which trips actually include the park?

[La Paz Waterfalls](/costa-rica/place/la-paz-waterfalls/) are in Costa Rica's mountainous Vara Blanca area. At La Paz Waterfall Gardens, pathways and stairs wind through humid forest to **5 waterfalls**. The grounds also feature a hummingbird garden and exhibits of birds, butterflies, frogs and other animals. For many travelers, it is their first encounter with the country's natural world after arriving in [San José](/costa-rica/place/san-jose/).

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} passing through La Paz. But the purpose and order of stops vary. Some programs visit the park after [Poás Volcano](/costa-rica/place/poas-volcano/); others stop before continuing to [Arenal](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/), while certain itineraries return to this area after boat trips through [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/).

**The key to choosing is the content of the entire sightseeing day and how much time is available for forest trails.** A “Poás — La Paz — Arenal” itinerary includes several major stops in one day. It offers varied experiences, but less time at each attraction than a dedicated visit to the nature park.

## Which Ada Tours itineraries include La Paz Waterfalls?

### 5 days: Tortuguero nature, Poás and the waterfalls

On the [“Costa Rica in 5 Days” tour](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-5-days/), the main nature experience takes place along Tortuguero's canals. Travelers then fly to San José for a sightseeing day visiting Poás National Park and La Paz Waterfall Gardens. At La Paz, there is a forest path to the waterfalls, lunch and an opportunity to see the hummingbird, bird, butterfly and frog exhibits.

This short trip suits visitors who want to combine forest canals with volcanic scenery without stretching their holiday across several weeks. But the schedule is full: flights and road transfers take up part of the day, so sightseeing time should be checked against the actual timetable.

### Another 5-day option: Tortuguero, coffee and La Paz

On [“Essential Costa Rica”](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-essentials/), the nature days in Tortuguero end with a return to the San José area. Guests then visit the [Doka coffee estate](/costa-rica/place/doka-estate/) and La Paz Gardens for lunch, a walk to the waterfalls and animal exhibits.

The difference from the preceding five-day trip is a stronger emphasis on coffee rather than visiting Poás Volcano on the same day. If volcanoes are important to you, do not assume these two offers are identical: compare the actual route and included stops.

### 7 days: Poás, La Paz, Arenal and Tamarindo beach

The [seven-day “Short but Complete Tour”](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-short-complete-tour/) begins with a trip from the international airport to Poás, La Paz Waterfalls and onward to the Arenal area. Over the following days, the route passes through [Caño Negro](/costa-rica/place/cano-negro-wildlife-refuge/), [Río Celeste](/costa-rica/place/rio-celeste/) and ends at [Tamarindo Beach](/costa-rica/place/playa-tamarindo/).

This itinerary is particularly dependent on arrival time: the first day includes multiple attractions and a long drive. Choose it if you want plenty of variety, but first establish whether the actual flights will allow the itinerary to proceed without rushing.

### 10 days: “Pearls of Costa Rica”

On the [“Pearls of Costa Rica” tour](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-pearls-10-days/), day two combines the Doka estate, Poás and La Paz. The journey then leads to Tortuguero, [Arenal](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/), [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/) and [Manuel Antonio](/costa-rica/place/manuel-antonio/).

La Paz remains one sightseeing stop within a broader nature itinerary. The ten-day journey appeals to travelers who want rainforests, volcanic landscapes, Caribbean canals and the wildlife of the Pacific coast. The extra days are allocated to other regions, so the overall duration does not itself mean a longer stay at the waterfalls.

### 10 days: “3 Perspectives on Costa Rica”

The [“3 Perspectives on Costa Rica” itinerary](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-3-perspectives/) combines the Doka coffee estate, Poás Volcano and La Paz Waterfalls with a transfer to Arenal. The active part of the trip is followed by time on the Pacific coast.

This combination suits visitors who want to experience the country's major natural contrasts without a separate multi-day trek near La Paz. If relaxing by the ocean after busy excursions is the main goal, compare beach time with the previous itinerary: the activities and sequence of regions differ.

### 16 days: an extensive private journey across Costa Rica

The [16-day premium Costa Rica tour](/costa-rica/tour/luxury-costa-rica-16-days/) includes an early nature-focused section featuring the Doka estate, Poás and La Paz. Later days take travelers through Tortuguero, Arenal, Monteverde, [Corcovado National Park](/costa-rica/place/corcovado-national-park/) and [Playa Conchal](/costa-rica/place/playa-conchal/).

This tour covers more ground and follows a private format. La Paz is an early stop, while most extra days are spent in other protected areas and along the coast. When choosing, check the actual accommodation, flights and excursions provided in the main itinerary.

### Combined with another country: Panama and Costa Rica

On the [10-day journey through Panama and Costa Rica](/multi-country/tour/panama-costa-rica/), travelers fly to Costa Rica after Panama City, visit Poás and explore La Paz Waterfall Gardens. The route continues around Arenal and later includes other natural areas of Costa Rica.

This option appeals to travelers who want to add the Panama Canal to volcanoes and forests. Allow for the international flight and sightseeing time on the arrival day. Do not automatically transfer the descriptions or terms of one country's itinerary to the other.

This table compares the content of the itineraries. Check admission tickets, lunches, individual transfers and guide services in each tour description. A program including La Paz does not necessarily cover every exhibit and service within the nature park.

## How La Paz Waterfall Gardens is organized

It is important to distinguish **the waterfalls as a natural attraction** from **La Paz Waterfall Gardens as a privately operated nature park**. Located in the forested Vara Blanca area, the park has a route past five waterfalls. According to the park's management, the walking trail network totals approximately **3.5 km**, and a quick visit requires at least **2 hours**. Exploring more trails and the animal exhibits thoroughly takes longer.

Paths wind through lush forest, with viewing platforms at different levels of the gorge. Some sections have stairs. Even if a photograph makes a waterfall appear close to the road, viewing several cascades takes time and involves walking. Visitors with reduced mobility should check accessible sections and whether stairs can be avoided.

The park has animal exhibits featuring birds, butterflies, frogs and big cats. Management describes the facility as **a center caring for rescued animals**, many of which were transferred by wildlife authorities and cannot be released into the wild. Visiting these exhibits should therefore not be presented as observing all these species in their natural forest habitat. Other destinations in our itineraries, such as [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/) and [Corcovado](/costa-rica/place/corcovado-national-park/), are better suited to watching wild animals in natural surroundings.

A separate [guide to La Paz Waterfalls](/costa-rica/place/la-paz-waterfalls/) introduces the attraction itself. When choosing a multi-day tour, the more important question is how much time that itinerary allocates to the park.

## Can La Paz be combined with Poás Volcano?

Yes. Several current Ada Tours itineraries explicitly combine the two. [Poás](/costa-rica/place/poas-volcano/) is part of a different protected area, the volcano's national park. Its main attraction is a crater with volcanic gases and characteristic highland landscapes. La Paz is in a forest zone where waterfalls and animals are the main highlights.

A route through both places shows the contrast between mountainous volcanic terrain and humid forest in one day. But it requires planning around weather, roads and the volcano's visiting arrangements. Poás National Park and the private La Paz Waterfall Gardens have separate admission systems; a ticket or entry to one does not automatically grant access to the other. Opening arrangements at Poás may change because of volcanic activity, so check official national park updates closer to departure.

If the route continues from La Paz to [La Fortuna and Arenal](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/), the sightseeing is followed by a drive and check-in at a new location. Assess this combination by departure time and the total number of stops, especially on arrival day.

## Weather, footwear and pace

Cloud forest and humid tropical forest occur in the La Paz area. Rain is possible in any season, and viewpoints, stairs and trails can be wet afterwards. Wear closed shoes with good grip, light rain protection and clothing comfortable for climbing stairs.

Across Costa Rica, the climate changes between highland areas, [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/), the tropical forests of [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/) and the ocean beaches of [Manuel Antonio](/costa-rica/place/manuel-antonio/). Pack for all stages rather than relying on the San José forecast alone.

A general overview of travel throughout the country is in our [Costa Rica guide](/costa-rica/). For waterfalls, volcanoes and forest scenery, explore [Costa Rica nature tours](/interests/nature/tours/costa-rica/). If observing animals in their natural habitat is your main goal, compare [Costa Rica wildlife tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/costa-rica/).

## Frequently asked questions about tours via La Paz

### How much time is needed at La Paz Waterfalls?

La Paz Waterfall Gardens recommends at least 2 hours for a quick visit. A leisurely walk past several cascades and all the exhibits you are interested in takes longer. When booking a multi-day journey, refer to the actual sightseeing day in its itinerary.

### Is La Paz a Costa Rican national park?

No. La Paz Waterfall Gardens is a privately operated nature park with waterfalls and an animal care center. It should not be confused with nearby [Poás Volcano National Park](/costa-rica/place/poas-volcano/).

### Do all tours visit La Paz and Poás on the same day?

No. Some itineraries combine them, including the [five-day tour](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-5-days/) and [“Pearls of Costa Rica”](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-pearls-10-days/). In [“Essential Costa Rica”](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-essentials/), the day is organized around the Doka estate and La Paz. Check the exact route.

### Is La Paz suitable for people who have difficulty walking?

The park has developed paths, but the route past several waterfalls includes stairs and changes in elevation. Before departure, check which viewing areas can be reached without walking the full route. A vehicle and guide do not eliminate the stairs inside the park.

### Where can I choose a tour with La Paz and time by the ocean?

They differ in duration, regions covered and time spent on the beaches.

## Liberia, Costa Rica: the White City and gateway to Guanacaste

**Liberia** is one of the principal cities of Guanacaste Province in northwestern [Costa Rica](/costa-rica/). For travelers, it often serves as a starting point: there is an international airport nearby, and the city provides access to national parks, volcanic scenery and the Pacific coast.

Liberia is also worth visiting in its own right. Its historic identity is associated with pale buildings and distinctive provincial architecture. The white facades gave the city its nickname, **Ciudad Blanca — the “White City.”**

## What to see in central Liberia

Old streets and light-colored houses recall Liberia's commercial and cultural role in the development of Guanacaste. As you walk around, look for single-story buildings, interior courtyards and the mixture of old and new architecture. The city also goes about its daily life as a regional center, with shops, restaurants, public spaces and transport services.

The **Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception** is a notable landmark in the center, as are the city's squares, which make pleasant stops during a transfer. A relaxed walk is enough to get an impression of the architecture, although you should not expect the same concentration of museums and colonial quarters as in Latin America's larger historic cities.

Liberia is particularly useful as a place to arrange an overnight stay, a transfer and practical travel needs before heading into the region's natural landscapes.

## Rincón de la Vieja National Park

One of the most interesting excursions from Liberia is to [Rincón de la Vieja](/costa-rica/place/rincon-de-la-vieja/). This volcanic area contains steam vents, bubbling mud pools and trails through different types of forest.

The national park has several visitor sectors with different access arrangements. **Las Pailas** is known for geothermal features and forest paths, while **Santa María** offers other routes and natural attractions.

SINAC warns that **access to the active crater may be closed due to volcanic activity**. Plan the trip around permitted and open nature trails rather than assuming a summit ascent is guaranteed. Seeing mud fields, forest and waterfalls matters more than attempting to reach a restricted area.

## Guanacaste beaches and the Nicoya Peninsula

From Liberia, you can continue to Guanacaste's Pacific coastline and beach areas. The style of holiday depends on where you stay: there are lively resorts as well as quieter stretches where the sea and natural surroundings are the main attraction.

Unlike the inland city, the beaches are some distance away and require a separate drive. When choosing a hotel, consider whether you need an urban transit stop, access to a national park or several days beside the water.

Guanacaste is particularly well suited to an itinerary that combines **volcanic scenery and the Pacific coast**. But a beach visit should not automatically be assumed to be included in every program starting at Liberia airport.

## Liberia airport and the start of a trip

Guanacaste International Airport near Liberia serves travelers arriving in northwestern Costa Rica. It enables itineraries to begin without passing through the capital, San José, when the main attractions lie in Guanacaste.

After landing, the route may continue directly to a nature park or to the coast. Travel time depends on the chosen hotel, road conditions and stops along the way.

Our [“5 Wonders of Costa Rica” tour](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-5-wonders/) **starts in Liberia**: on day one, you arrive at the international airport, are met and transferred to Rincón de la Vieja. The following days take you through other natural parts of the country.

This shows how Liberia can serve as an entry point. [Other Costa Rica tours](/costa-rica/tour/) sometimes start in San José, so choose the airport based on the actual itinerary.

## Combining the city, national park and coast

For a brief stopover, arrival, a walk around the center and an overnight stay may be enough. A national park visit requires a separate day allowing for the drive, admission and the length of your chosen trail. If Guanacaste's beaches are the goal, plan additional time on the coast.

The region can be hot and sunny in the dry season. Bring water, sun protection and walking shoes; comfortable closed shoes are needed for forest trails. Follow warnings from conservation staff when visiting volcanic attractions.

## Frequently asked questions about Liberia

### Why is Liberia called the White City?

The nickname comes from the city's light-colored house facades and historic architecture.

### Does Liberia have an airport?

Yes. An international airport near the city is used for travel to Guanacaste and northwestern Costa Rica.

### Where can you see bubbling volcanic mud pools?

They are in [Rincón de la Vieja National Park](/costa-rica/place/rincon-de-la-vieja/), not in central Liberia. Different park sectors may have their own rules and restrictions.

### Which Ada Tours trip starts in Liberia?

[“5 Wonders of Costa Rica”](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-5-wonders/) begins with arrival at Liberia airport and a transfer to Rincón de la Vieja.

## Tours through Liberia: Guanacaste airport, volcanoes and the ocean

[Liberia](/costa-rica/place/liberia/) is a city in Guanacaste Province in northwestern Costa Rica. Daniel Oduber International Airport is located here, making it convenient to begin a journey toward [Rincón de la Vieja](/costa-rica/place/rincon-de-la-vieja/) Volcano and then travel through the mountainous interior toward the [Pacific coast](/costa-rica/place/pacific-coast/).

Our catalog lists {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} passing through Liberia. **In our itineraries, the city mainly serves as the arrival and departure point**, rather than a standalone multi-day sightseeing destination. After the airport, travelers head toward Rincón de la Vieja and return to Liberia toward the end of the journey.

This matters when choosing a tour: if you want to see Liberia's historic center and traditional architecture, you will need to set aside time for it. The city's appearance on an itinerary does not mean such a walk is included. Read more on the [Liberia city page](/costa-rica/place/liberia/), or compare actual multi-day trips below.

## Which itineraries begin and end in Liberia?

### “5 Wonders of Costa Rica”: 9 days of nature and activities

The [“5 Wonders of Costa Rica” tour](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-5-wonders/) begins with arrival in Liberia. After meeting guests at the airport, the transfer heads to [Rincón de la Vieja](/costa-rica/place/rincon-de-la-vieja/) and Hacienda Guachipelín. The following day features the Mega Combo Tour: hanging bridges, a cable car, horseback riding, a waterfall and hot springs.

The itinerary continues to [Río Celeste](/costa-rica/place/rio-celeste/) in the [Tenorio National Park](/costa-rica/place/tenorio-volcano-national-park/) area, an introduction to Maleku culture, and [La Fortuna and Arenal Volcano](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/). After crossing Lake Arenal, travelers visit [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/), where a canopy tour above the cloud forest is scheduled. The final section is for time on the coast, with a transfer to Liberia airport on day 9.

This option suits travelers who want to explore several natural regions and try a range of activities in 9 days. **A Russian-speaking guide is expressly listed among the included services** in this program. When comparing it with another journey, pay attention to the complete set of excursions and guiding arrangements.

### “Beach and Mountain Holiday”: 9 days with a more athletic excursion

The [“Beach and Mountain Holiday” tour](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-beaches-mountains/) also starts and finishes at Liberia airport. On day one, guests transfer to Rincón de la Vieja, with no mandatory excursions after landing. Day two features a canopy experience, canyon descent in Río Blanco, tubing down the Río Negro through **Class II rapids**, horseback riding and relaxation in hot springs with mud baths.

The trip then continues via the [Tenorio](/costa-rica/place/tenorio-volcano-national-park/) region and [Río Celeste](/costa-rica/place/rio-celeste/), a Maleku village, and [Arenal](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/) with Mistico hanging bridges and the Arenal Volcano 1968 trail. The transfer to [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/) uses the Taxi-Boat-Taxi route: vehicle, boat across the lake and another vehicle. A free day on the northern Pacific coast precedes the return flight.

Here, **the day around Rincón de la Vieja is specifically designed as a sports and adventure program**. Compared with “5 Wonders,” this is a significant distinction, especially for people who prefer gentle walks to more demanding activities. Similar place names do not make the included excursions identical.

To compare prices, open both itineraries and review hotels, excursions, guide language, admission tickets and meals. Do not assume any price difference is simply a surcharge for comfort: first compare what each trip provides.

## Why does the journey start in Liberia rather than San José?

Daniel Oduber Airport in Liberia is located in Guanacaste Province. It is distinct from Juan Santamaría International Airport, which serves the [San José](/costa-rica/place/san-jose/) area. For routes beginning around Rincón de la Vieja and ending on the northern coast, flying through Liberia reduces the need to cross much of the country just to use the capital's airport.

**Check the airport code on your ticket:** Liberia uses LIR; the international airport near San José uses SJO. If you independently book a flight into a different airport, the transfer included in your tour may not be suitable; extra transportation or an itinerary change may be needed.

Both of our trips include a meeting on arrival in Liberia and a transfer back to the airport at the end of the route. These are confirmed terms of these specific programs, not an indication that every Costa Rica tour starts in Guanacaste.

If your arrival time is inconvenient, or you want a separate walk around the city, arrange this when planning your journey. A “Liberia” stop at the start of day one is primarily a transport stage.

## What lies between Liberia and the coast?

The first nature stop is [Rincón de la Vieja](/costa-rica/place/rincon-de-la-vieja/), an area of volcanic mountains and national parkland with steam vents, hot springs and forest trails. According to official information from conservation authority SINAC, the Las Pailas sector has a circular route past fumaroles and bubbling mud pools. However, resort-run activities and national park trails are different products: the inclusion of a Rincón de la Vieja excursion does not mean every trail within the national park is covered.

The second nature-focused stage features [Tenorio](/costa-rica/place/tenorio-volcano-national-park/) and the bright-blue [Río Celeste](/costa-rica/place/rio-celeste/). The main attractions here are forest walks and the volcanic landscape. Later, around [Arenal](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/), you can experience rainforest, hanging bridges and old lava fields. [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/) is different again, with cloud forest and a cooler, damp climate.

Both itineraries conclude on the [Pacific coast](/costa-rica/place/pacific-coast/). “5 Wonders” specifies accommodation near Tamarindo, while the other trip stays on the northern coast. Much of this portion is free time. **Which beach, hotel and services are included** must be checked separately for each tour.

## Physical activity, weather and preparation

Northwestern Costa Rica has distinct, more dry and more rainy seasons. Yet during a nine-day itinerary, travelers change altitude and natural regions several times: from hot Guanacaste to humid forest, volcanoes and misty Monteverde. You will need clothing suitable for both warm ocean weather and cooler, rainy mountain walks.

Wear closed shoes with good grip for volcano and forest trails. For the water activities in the second program, check fitness requirements, safety equipment and the operator's restrictions for your chosen date. Class II rapids should not be treated as equivalent to a gentle boat ride.

Rincón de la Vieja National Park is managed by SINAC, and its visitor sectors have their own rules and booking system. Check access arrangements and weather restrictions before traveling. This is particularly important if you want to add an independent visit to the main itinerary.

For more options, see our [Costa Rica tours catalog](/costa-rica/tour/), while the [country guide](/costa-rica/) explains the geography and seasons.

## Frequently asked questions about tours through Liberia

### Do both itineraries include sightseeing in Liberia?

No. In both trips, Liberia is mainly the city of the international airport: arrival, meeting, transfer to Rincón de la Vieja and return for departure. To explore the city center, you need extra time. Read more on the [Liberia page](/costa-rica/place/liberia/).

### Do both tours have the same duration?

Yes. [“5 Wonders of Costa Rica”](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-5-wonders/) and [“Beach and Mountain Holiday”](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-beaches-mountains/) are both 9 days and 8 nights long. Similar geography does not rule out important differences in activities and conditions.

### Which tour should I choose to avoid demanding water activities?

Start by considering [“5 Wonders”](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-5-wonders/): it lists hanging bridges, a cable car, horseback riding and hot springs. However, it also includes active excursions, so assess your fitness and check restrictions. The other tour specifically includes tubing down the Río Negro.

### Can I fly into San José and join a tour via Liberia?

The itinerary could theoretically be renegotiated, but this is not the standard arrival point listed in either program. Check extra transfers, travel time and who pays for them before buying flights. Do not assume such a change is already included.

### Is there time for a beach holiday?

Yes. Both nine-day itineraries devote their final days to the [northern Pacific coast](/costa-rica/place/pacific-coast/) and free time. Check the exact beach, hotel and duration of the seaside stay in the selected program.
